question.problem:
Which of the following could be matrices of quadratic forms defined on ${R}^{3}?$

$$
T=[\begin{aligned}4 & 5 & -3 \\ 5 & 1 & -8 \\ -3 & -8 & 7\end{aligned}],\,U=[\begin{aligned}7 & 1 & -2 \\ 1 & 4 & 5 \\ -2 & 5 & 7\end{aligned}],\,V=[\begin{aligned}1 & -3 \\ -3 & 1\end{aligned}]
$$
question.worked_solution:
Recall that every quadratic form defined on ${R}^{3}$ has an associated $3\times 3$ symmetric matrix.

With that in mind, let's examine each matrix in turn.

- $T$ could be a matrix of a quadratic form defined on ${R}^{3}$ since it is a $3\times 3$ symmetric matrix.

- $U$ could also be a matrix of a quadratic form defined on ${R}^{3}$ since it is a $3\times 3$ symmetric matrix.

- $V$ *cannot* be a matrix of a quadratic form defined on ${R}^{3}$ since it's a $2\times 2$ matrix (not $3\times 3$).

Therefore, the correct answer is "$T$ and $U$ only."
